It also does not show whether "members" was used in a defined sense (for example, plan enrollees) that "individuals" might broaden. Because this is a narrative description section, that effect seems unlikely.

llm.path: Medical Records Documentation Used for Reviews

answer.what_changed: Before: "Medical records documentation is required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage". After: "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage". The words "is" were removed and "may be" added; the rest of the section text is identical.
answer.interpretation: The change moves medical records documentation from a firm requirement to a conditional one. This could mean documentation is no longer always needed for coverage review, or that it is only requested in some cases. That might affect what providers must submit or retain. It could also be a softening of boilerplate with no practical change in how reviews are run.
answer.uncertainty: The text does not say when or under what conditions documentation would be required, nor whether review practice actually changes. It does not state which plan types, products or populations this applies to. The referenced guidelines, Medical Records Documentation Used for Reviews, are not shown and may define the actual requirements.
answer.suggested_next_step: Check the referenced Medical Records Documentation Used for Reviews guidelines and the policy's change summary to see whether documentation requirements actually changed. Then confirm with the payer or the plan's documentation rules before relaxing any internal documentation practices.
